requirements.text: The explorer supports create file, create folder, rename, move, delete and drag-and-drop (dropping an item onto a folder moves it there) for both files and folders. Delete asks for confirmation naming the item (and, for a folder, that everything inside goes with it) and sends the item to the Recycle Bin. If the Recycle Bin cannot take the item, the delete is refused with a message and nothing is permanently deleted. A name clash is refused with a clear message and nothing is overwritten. Moving a folder into itself or one of its descendants is refused. Renaming or moving a file that is open re-points its tab to the new path and recomputes the tab groups; the same applies to every open file under a renamed or moved folder. Deleting an item closes its open tabs, and any unsaved-changes warning is folded into the single delete confirmation. After any operation the affected folder level is refreshed. In the window this is the explorer panel's actions; in the core it is four file operations (create, rename, move and delete) that extend the explorer's existing folder-listing commands and the editor's existing store rather than a new backend module.

requirements.text: Every terminal has an executable flag that is on by default, is saved with the terminal, and can be turned off or on where terminals are edited. Non-executable terminals are not started or stopped by the window's Start all / Stop all action or by F5, but can still be started and stopped individually with their own controls. The Start all / Stop all button state and the app status indicator count only executable terminals. A saved terminal that has no flag loads as executable. The engine and tdk 'up' action is not part of this revision and keeps its current behaviour.

requirements.text: Refresh is available only from the Utilities menu refresh item, the git bar refresh button and the command palette 'Refresh everything' entry. No keyboard shortcut performs refresh. The command palette 'Refresh everything' entry shows a clear 'No shortcut' note in place of a shortcut key, consistent with the accepted palette rule that every app-level command shows its real shortcut or a clear 'No shortcut' note. No menu, tooltip or help text advertises F5 as refresh. Where a Start all / Stop all control shows a key hint, it shows F5.

requirements.text: The explorer supports create file, create folder, rename, move, delete and drag-and-drop (dropping an item onto a folder moves it there) for both files and folders. Delete asks for confirmation naming the item (and, for a folder, that everything inside goes with it) and sends the item to the Recycle Bin. If the Recycle Bin cannot take the item, the delete is refused with a message and nothing is permanently deleted. A name clash is refused with a clear message and nothing is overwritten. Moving a folder into itself or one of its descendants is refused. Renaming or moving a file that is open re-points its tab to the new path and recomputes the tab groups; the same applies to every open file under a renamed or moved folder. Deleting an item closes its open tabs, and any unsaved-changes warning is folded into the single delete confirmation. After any operation the affected folder level is refreshed. In the window this is the explorer panel's actions; in the core it is four file operations (create, rename, move and delete) that extend the explorer's existing folder-listing commands and the editor's existing store rather than a new backend module.

requirements.text: The command palette stays a palette and receives a mobile-first, desktop-aware layout pass. On a narrow, mobile-width viewport it fills the available width and sits near the top so the on-screen keyboard does not squeeze the list; on a desktop-width viewport it keeps its current look.
tests: R10: the mobile-first base fills the width, sits at the top and is viewport-bounded
R10: a desktop media query restores the current centred 560px palette
R10: a long command label truncates inside the panel instead of overflowing it

requirements.text: Every terminal has an executable flag that is on by default, is saved with the terminal, and can be turned off or on where terminals are edited. Non-executable terminals are not started or stopped by the window's Start all / Stop all action or by F5, but can still be started and stopped individually with their own controls. The Start all / Stop all button state and the app status indicator count only executable terminals. A saved terminal that has no flag loads as executable. The engine and tdk 'up' action is not part of this revision and keeps its current behaviour.

R11: a non-executable terminal keeps its name, command and remove controls
R11: a newly added terminal is executable by default
R11: a missing saved flag reads as executable and only an explicit false turns it off

requirements.text: Refresh is available only from the Utilities menu refresh item, the git bar refresh button and the command palette 'Refresh everything' entry. No keyboard shortcut performs refresh. The command palette 'Refresh everything' entry shows a clear 'No shortcut' note in place of a shortcut key, consistent with the accepted palette rule that every app-level command shows its real shortcut or a clear 'No shortcut' note. No menu, tooltip or help text advertises F5 as refresh. Where a Start all / Stop all control shows a key hint, it shows F5.

R12: Start all and Stop all show F5 while Refresh everything shows No shortcut
